## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

Write what you want in an issue and add the `OpenCode` label. OpenCode checks out the project, uses the shared skills, builds the experience, runs tests, verifies the result, and publishes an immutable OmGithub project link from the finished commit. Yes, it creates the code. Yes, it runs the verification loop. Yes, it can expose the result in a temporary browser URL. ## 🧠 TL;DR 1. Open a GitHub issue. 2. Describe the game or app you want. 3. GitHub Actions handles the runner, OpenCode handles implementation, and the workflow handles verification plus the immutable project commit. To run against an existing non-default branch, end the issue title with a `branch: ` directive. The directive selects the checkout and is removed before the issue body is sent to OpenCode: ```sh gh issue create \ --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub \ --title "Custom branch smoke test branch: codex/omgithub-site" \ --body "Build a tiny browser page." \ --label Goal \ --label OpenCode ``` The GitHub App validates the branch before dispatching. ## Objective
- Build a polished 3D Subway Surfers-style endless runner with three lanes, running in the browser.

## Requirements
- User request was only: `"3D Subway Surfers endless runner with three lanes"`.
- Must support desktop and mobile, including usable touch controls and safe-area-aware layouts.
- Existing repo was effectively empty aside from runtime/tooling files; no framework constraints were given.

## Decisions
- Vanilla JavaScript + Three.js (`three@0.187.0`) with Vite (`vite@8.3.5`).
- Original game branding: **Metro Rush**, with a sunset low-poly city/subway visual direction.
- Mechanics implemented: three lanes, jump, roll/slide, procedural endless obstacle and coin generation, speed scaling, score/distance/coin HUD, persistent local best, pause/resume, game-over/retry/home, sound toggle.
- Procedural Web Audio music/SFX, no external audio assets.
- Mobile controls: swipe gestures plus on-screen left/right/jump/roll buttons.
- Performance is critical because Chromium runs under software `llvmpipe`; optimization work has focused on reducing DOM repaints, draw calls, shadows, lights, and merged/instanced geometry.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created full project scaffold: `index.html`, `src/style.css`, `src/main.js`, `src/audio.js`, `src/environment.js`, `src/player.js`, `src/obstacles.js`.
- Built stylized original runner character with animated run/jump/slide/crash poses.
- Built procedural city, rails, sleepers, lamps, gantries, catenary wires, clouds, dust, sky shader, sun, and fog.
- Implemented trains, barriers, overhead gates, coins, magnet power-ups, particles, collisions, and scoring.
- Implemented menus/HUD/how-to-play/pause/game-over screens, keyboard/swipe/touch controls, localStorage best score.
- Added local Bungee/Space Grotesk fonts under `src/fonts/`.
- Verified visual screenshots in `screenshots/menu2.png` and `screenshots/game2.png` look polished and recognizably subway-surf-style.
- Major performance improvements:
  - Removed shadows, `PCFSoftShadowMap`, per-building point lights, backdrop filters, mix-blend modes, and animated grain.
  - Reduced render resolution for software rendering (`renderScale = 0.58`, `maxRenderWidth = 860`).
  - Instanced buildings, roofs, and signs.
  - Merged rails, track chunk lamp/cabinet geometry, gantries, catenary wires.
  - Merged train/barrier/gate geometry.
  - Converted coins to a single `InstancedMesh` pool.
  - Throttled HUD updates to 10 Hz and added a menu render freeze after the first static menu frame.
- Latest draw-call state: menu ~137 calls, gameplay ~210–215 calls; runtime has no current page errors after geometry merge fix.

### Active
- Tune and verify performance after recent obstacle instancing/merging changes.
- Capture fresh desktop gameplay screenshots after optimization because existing screenshots predate obstacle optimization.
- Confirm game state advances correctly under software rendering and collision/gameplay remain functional.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run a fresh Playwright check/screenshot with a longer wait and inspect `screenshots/` for current gameplay visuals.
2. Measure FPS/draw calls in menu and gameplay after HUD throttling; target at least low double-digit gameplay FPS under `llvmpipe`.
3. If FPS is still low, reduce player/character draw calls and/or reduce visible prefill obstacles; potentially reduce HUD compositing further.
4. Test lane switching, jump, slide, coin collection, magnet pickup, crash/game-over, restart, pause/resume, and mobile viewport/touch controls.
5. Run `npm run build` and inspect desktop + 390x844 mobile screenshots.
6. Fix visual regressions: menu has a bright fog/orange gap to the right of the side buildings; consider strengthening city silhouette/ground/background.
7. Commit only after final browser verification; all changes are currently uncommitted.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/main.js`: game loop, state, camera, HUD throttling, input, menu freeze, screenshots/debug global.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/obstacles.js`: trains, barriers, gates, instanced coins, particles, patterns, collisions.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/environment.js`: city/track/sky/lighting and instancing/merging optimizations.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/player.js`: character model and movement animation.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/audio.js`: procedural music and SFX.

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

## Metro Rush

A polished three-lane 3D endless runner set on a sunset city subway line. Dodge trains, jump barriers, roll under gates, and collect coins while the pace builds.

### Play

```bash
npm install
npm run dev
```

Open the printed local URL. To build the static site:

```bash
npm run build
npm run preview
```

### Controls

- **Desktop:** `←` / `→` or `A` / `D` to switch lanes, `↑` / `W` / `Space` to jump, `↓` / `S` to roll, `Esc` / `P` to pause.
- **Touch:** swipe left, right, up, or down, or use the four on-screen buttons.
- **Audio:** use the speaker button in the HUD to mute or unmute the procedural soundtrack and effects.

Best scores are stored locally in the browser. The layout respects mobile safe areas and switches to larger touch targets on coarse pointers.
